paragraphs: A god and a demon once went to a great sage to learn about the Self. They stayed and studied with him for a long time. At last the sage told them that they themselves were the very Being they were looking for.

Both of them took this to mean that the body was the Self. They went home delighted and told their people they had learned all there was to learn: eat, drink and enjoy, for we are the Self and nothing exists beyond us.
The demon, whose nature was dull and clouded, never questioned this. He was perfectly happy believing that he was God and that the Self simply meant the body.

The god had a purer nature. At first he too thought, I am this body, so I must keep it strong, healthy, well dressed and full of pleasures. But within a few days he sensed that his master could not have meant that. Bodies die, and the Self cannot die. He went back and asked. The sage only said, find out for yourself; you are That.

So the god searched deeper. Perhaps the vital forces that run the body were the Self? But they grew strong when he ate and weak when he fasted. He returned, and again the sage told him to discover it himself. Next he guessed it was the mind, yet he soon saw that thoughts kept changing, good one moment and bad the next. The mind was far too unsteady. Once more the sage gave the same reply.

Finally, through his own seeking, the god realised that he was the Self: beyond thought, unborn and undying, untouched by sword, fire, wind or water, without beginning or end, all-knowing and all-powerful, beyond both body and mind. He found peace. The demon, attached to his body, never reached the truth.

Swamiji observed that the world has many such demonic natures, and a few godly ones too. Offer to teach people how to enjoy their senses more and crowds will gather. Offer to show them the highest goal and few will come. Fewer still can grasp it, and fewer still have the patience to reach it.
learn: The first easy answer is rarely the deepest one. Like the god, keep questioning, testing and returning to your teachers until you really understand. Curiosity plus patience is what separates surface knowledge from real insight.
